subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should plugin/external recurring cron jobs be allowed to auto-enable and inherit agent/default models, or must core require explicit activation, explicit model selection, and cost/quota policy before first run?
rationale: The fix changes cron activation defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, and provider-spend guardrails; source shows the problem remains, but automation cannot choose the acceptable compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Require activation and explicit model policy
options.body: Default externally or plugin-created recurring agent-turn jobs to a pending/disabled state, require operator activation or an explicit per-job model before running, and add cost/quota guardrails through the related cron-budget policy work.

options.title: Narrow Model-Cost Guard
options.body: Keep current activation behavior but warn or block recurring agentTurn jobs that inherit an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split Into Follow-Ups
options.body: Use the related open issues for circuit breakers, budgets, and provenance while keeping this issue as the consent/default-model cluster index.

recommendation.title: Require activation and explicit model policy
recommendation.body: Default externally or plugin-created recurring agent-turn jobs to a pending/disabled state, require operator activation or an explicit per-job model before running, and add cost/quota guardrails through the related cron-budget policy work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest verified routing evidence is cron model-selection and agent default/fallback history near the inherited-model behavior.
